prompt:
Automatic retries (the worker endpoints `POST /jobs/:id/start` and
`POST /jobs/:id/fail`) don't follow the job's retry policy.

Job `sync` has `retry: { maxAttempts: 3, backoff: "1s", maxBackoff: "5m" }`. From the
worker log:

    08:00:00  run 1 failed -> API requeued it with retryAt 08:00:02
    08:00:02  run 2 failed -> retryAt 08:00:06

The policy says the first retry waits `backoff` (1s), then the delay doubles up to
`maxBackoff`, so we expected 08:00:01 and 08:00:03. `maxAttempts` is the total number of
runs including the first one; once they are used up the job must end up `failed`
instead of being requeued.

Also, while a retry is pending, `GET /jobs/:id` reports `nextRunAt` from the job's
schedule (or `null` for unscheduled jobs) instead of the retry time, so the dashboard
shows the wrong "next run".

setup.replace:
import { canTransition } from "../../core/src/lifecycle.ts";
import { nextAttemptAt } from "../../core/src/retry.ts";

nextRunAt: string | null; // when the job runs next; a pending retry comes first
  retryAt: string | null;

setup.find: nextRunAt: parsed && active ? nextRun(parsed, now).toISOString() : null,
setup.replace:
nextRunAt: parsed && active ? nextRun(parsed, now).toISOString() : null,
    retryAt: job.retryAt ?? null,

setup.find: import { cancelJob, createJob, getJob, listJobs, retryJob } from "./jobs.ts";
setup.replace: import { cancelJob, createJob, failJob, getJob, listJobs, retryJob, startJob, succeedJob } from "./jobs.ts";

.add("POST", "/jobs/:id/retry", scoped("jobs:write", (_req, p) => retryJob(ctx, p.id)))
    .add("POST", "/jobs/:id/start", scoped("jobs:write", (_req, p) => startJob(ctx, p.id)))
    .add("POST", "/jobs/:id/fail", scoped("jobs:write", (req, p) => failJob(ctx, p.id, req)))
    .add("POST", "/jobs/:id/succeed", scoped("jobs:write", (_req, p) => succeedJob(ctx, p.id)));

solution.find: nextRunAt: parsed && active ? nextRun(parsed, now).toISOString() : null,
solution.replace: nextRunAt: active && job.retryAt ? job.retryAt : parsed && active ? nextRun(parsed, now).toISOString() : null,
